question: One gigabyte (GB) is equal to (in binary):
solution:
The correct answer is __**1,048,576 kilobyte**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **1 gigabyte (GB) is equal to 1,024 megabytes** **(MB) **in binary notation, which is the standard used in computer science.
 
• The binary system is based on powers of 2, hence 1 GB equals 2³⁰ bytes.
 
• **1 megabytes (MB)**** is equal to 1,024 kilobytes** **(KB) **in binary, making a gigabyte significantly larger than a kilobyte.
 
• The term gigabyte is often used to measure storage capacity in computers, such as hard drives, SSDs, and USB flash drives.
 
• This binary measurement is different from the decimal system used by manufacturers, where 1 GB equals 1,000,000,000 bytes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A **byte **contains **8 bits**.
 
• 256 different values are represented by a single byte.
 
• To **store a single character**, the byte was originally created.
 
• To represent all uppercase and lowercase letters, 256 values are required.
 
• Few bytes of data may be contained by the small plain text.
 
• To measure specific data within the file, a byte is used.
 
• 1024 bytes is contained by the** 1 kilobyte**.
